taxonomy.subtopic: TSC1/TSC2 loss and constitutive mTOR signaling

questions.stem_html:
A 7-year-old girl has seizures, developmental delay, hypopigmented ash-leaf macules, facial angiofibromas, and a shagreen patch. Brain MRI shows cortical tubers, and renal imaging shows bilateral angiomyolipomas. Genetic testing reveals loss of function in TSC2.

Which signaling abnormality promotes these lesions?

options.text_html: Failure to activate RAS prevents MAP-kinase signaling
Constitutive degradation of beta-catenin blocks cellular proliferation
Failure to inhibit Rheb leads to constitutive activation of mTOR complex 1
Inactivation of hypoxia-inducible factor reduces vascular growth
Excess PTEN activity suppresses PI3K-AKT signaling

questions.explanation_html: The hamartin-tuberin complex normally inhibits the small GTPase Rheb. Loss of TSC1 or TSC2 leaves Rheb active and chronically stimulates mTORC1-dependent cell growth. The multisystem hamartomas of tuberous sclerosis arise from loss of a tumor-suppressor brake on mTOR signaling.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: TSC loss increases growth signaling; it does not suppress RAS as the central mechanism.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Blocking beta-catenin would reduce rather than promote hamartomatous growth.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: VHL loss, not TSC2 loss, stabilizes HIF; reduced HIF does not explain this syndrome.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Increased PTEN would restrain growth, whereas TSC1/TSC2 loss releases mTOR inhibition.

questions.educational_objective: Connect TSC1/TSC2 loss to Rheb activation, constitutive mTORC1 signaling, and multisystem hamartomas.
